answer: Station a zephyr on every connection: a soft, time-varying signal that the network sends each head individually, and the head must echo it back signed over the exact waveform it heard. Because the wave differs per recipient and shifts within the epoch, a pre-recorded echo cannot be replayed, and a farm cannot copy one valid response across its shells. A gale then sweeps the register each epoch: any identity whose echo fails to verify is struck wholly, so keeping hundreds of dormant clones alive costs a fresh live exchange apiece.
